justifications.functional_suitability: All functional requirements are comprehensively met: SFU Video Container and Resilient Video Client Component handle consultations (R-01), E-Prescription Routing Component handles prescriptions (R-02), AI Symptom Checker Container provides urgency recommendations (R-03), and IAM / Consent Service with Consent Engine manages granular patient consent (R-04).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance is optimized via Regional Memorystore for deduplication, Async Event Broker using Google Cloud Pub/Sub for asynchronous message handling, and Adaptive Bitrate Controller with Resilient Video Client Component adjusting WebRTC streams to handle constrained network bandwidth effectively.
justifications.compatibility: Compatibility is explicitly addressed: Interoperability & Translation Component and External Pharmacies integrate via HL7 FHIR and regional REST/SOAP standards. In addition, IAM / Consent Service seamlessly federates with eIDAS and OAuth2/OIDC Identity Providers.
justifications.usability: Both Patients and Licensed Clinicians are provided tailored user interfaces via Web App & Mobile App. Usability in rural or international settings is reinforced by Localization & a11y Provider Component and Offline-First Symptom Module Component.
justifications.reliability: Reliability targets are met through Adaptive Bitrate Controller and Resilient Video Client Component enabling degraded operation below 300 kbit/s. Fault tolerance is bolstered by DLQ Manager in Async Event Broker and circuit breaking across Envoy API Gateways.
justifications.security: Data residency is strictly partitioned between EU and US API Gateways and Cloud SQL with CMEK. Policy Enforcement Interceptor and Consent Ledger enforce access boundaries, while Audit & Telemetry Logger captures MLflow model versions and inputs for traceability.
justifications.maintainability: The C4 architecture demonstrates high modularity and separation of concerns across decoupled containers (Core Services, SFU Video Container, AI Symptom Checker Container) with well-defined gRPC/mTLS interfaces, enabling independent testing, deployment, and maintainability of domain modules.
justifications.portability: Portability is thoroughly addressed by distributing standardized Envoy gateways across europe-west3 and us-central1 on GCP, while isolating cloud-native dependencies (Cloud SQL, Secret Manager, Pub/Sub) behind portable containerized runtimes like LiveKit, Spring Boot, and FastAPI.

PERF-01.justification: SFU video containers and adaptive media routers support WebRTC load, but cluster autoscaling and TURN relay bandwidth capacity during sudden 5,000 EU session spikes lack explicit scaling elasticity specifications.
sensitivity_points: Media router socket limits and coturn relay bandwidth under concurrent EU loads
tradeoffs: SFU media proxying improves stream coordination but increases server compute and memory footprint

PERF-02.justification: Handling ~14 requests/sec (50k/hour) is well within PyTorch container capacity. Asynchronous MLflow telemetry offloads logging latency, allowing inference pipelines to return recommendations under 3 seconds reliably.
sensitivity_points: PyTorch model execution time and async audit queue ingestion throughput
tradeoffs: Asynchronous telemetry logging reduces inference latency but risks audit delays during system crashes

AVAIL-01.justification: Adaptive Bitrate Controller and Resilient Video Client dynamically downscale stream quality below 300 kbit/s. Independent Clinical Documentation endpoints ensure notes are preserved without dropped consultations.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic WebRTC bandwidth probing and graceful audio-only codec degradation
tradeoffs: Aggressive video stream degradation preserves call connectivity at the expense of visual clarity

AVAIL-02.justification: Target cloud specifies only us-central1 for the US. If the entire US region fails, no secondary US region exists to restore services without violating strict EU data residency constraints.
sensitivity_points: Absence of secondary US failover region while strictly maintaining geographic data residency
tradeoffs: Strict regional data confinement prevents cross-region EU failover when US outages occur

MOD-01.justification: The modular architecture contains an explicit Interoperability & Translation Component combined with E-Prescription Routing, isolating new national e-prescription protocol adapters without affecting core business domains.
sensitivity_points: Extensibility and isolation of country-specific e-prescription protocol translation adapters
tradeoffs: Centralizing integration adapters adds an abstraction layer but simplifies multi-national protocol maintenance

MOD-02.justification: The AI container incorporates MLflow Tracking Client and model artifact storage, ensuring every recommendation links to model version hashes and allows runtime rollbacks without service interruption.
sensitivity_points: Traceability linkage between logged recommendation records and model registry artifact versions
tradeoffs: Logging explicit model version tags with each inference adds storage metadata overhead

SEC-01.justification: Policy Enforcement Interceptors, Regional API Gateways, and Consent Engines enforce regional isolation. Data Access Proxies utilize row-level security and CMEK to block unauthorized cross-region clinician access.
sensitivity_points: Zero-trust token validation and PostgreSQL row-level security policy evaluation on cross-border queries
tradeoffs: Enforcing zero-trust consent validation on every query increases backend request evaluation latency

SEC-02.justification: Withdrawing consent writes to immutable Consent Ledgers and instantly purges the Revocation Cache Redis component. Policy Enforcement Interceptors and Data Access Proxies enforce this revocation immediately.
sensitivity_points: Propagation latency between consent ledger updates and regional Redis cache invalidation
tradeoffs: Immediate cache invalidation ensures zero propagation delay but increases initial database read load
